content: The most common causes of monogenic diabetes are outlined in Table 2.6 of the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines. Genetic counseling is strongly recommended for families with a documented history of monogenic diabetes. This counseling serves to provide guidance on appropriate treatment options and to help families understand the inheritance patterns of the condition. An accurate diagnosis of monogenic diabetes is critical, as it can significantly influence the management and prevention of both microvascular complications, such as retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy, and macrovascular complications, including cardiovascular disease.
